                    ANCHORAGE, ALASKA
                    AR No. 2023-260(S)*
 1  A RESOLUTION OF THE ANCHORAGE ASSEMBLY RECOGNIZING THE
 2  COMMUNITY’S DIVERSE LIVED EXPERIENCES OF HOUSING  IN THE
 3   MUNICIPALITY OF ANCHORAGE AND ADOPTING GENERAL PRINCIPLES
 4  FOR FUTURE HOUSING POLICY DECISIONS.
 5
 6  WHEREAS, the community of Anchorage was founded in 1915 as a tent city on the
 7   unceded lands of the Dena’ina Athabascan people, and grew in less than 100 years
 8    to have a population of almost 300,000 residents; and
 9
10  WHEREAS, the community has faced many housing stresses in its history, from
11   housing shortages during periods of prosperity and rapid growth, to mass out-
12   migrations during recessions, and now a lack of supply and diversity of housing
13   stock to meet the changing demands of our population; and
14
15  WHEREAS, as the community grows and changes over time, it becomes a better
16   place as a direct result of the collective hard work, investments, innovations, and
17    creativity of the diverse people who make Anchorage their home; and
18
19  WHEREAS, a home takes many forms, but is in essence a place where a person
20    feels safe, where a person can rest, and serves as a stable anchoring point in a
21   person’s life, regardless of the many challenges they may face; and
22
23  WHEREAS, housing also takes many forms, from modest to grand, from large to
24   small, owned and rented, old and new, in urban neighborhoods and rural areas; and
25
26  WHEREAS, some residents in our community live in the same home they grew up
27    in, or has been owned by multiple generations of their family; and
28
29  WHEREAS, some community residents chose their home because of the amenities
30   and features of the surrounding neighborhood; and
31
32  WHEREAS, some residents live in neighborhoods they could afford when they
33  moved in, but would not be able to afford a similar home today; and
34
35  WHEREAS, some residents  live  in  their ideal home  for  their employment or
36   profession, family size, life stage, or personal preferences; and
37
38  WHEREAS, some residents’ homes do not meet their needs; and
39
40  WHEREAS, some residents can only afford a home by living with roommates; and
41
42  WHEREAS, some residents cannot afford housing, even if they are employed; and
43
44  WHEREAS, some residents live in unsafe places, but have few or no alternatives

AR 2023-260(S): adopting principles to guide housing policy decisions                     Page 2 of 3


 1   they can afford in order to better their situation; and
 2
 3  WHEREAS, some residents have had housing, but were evicted because they could
 4   not continue to afford rent; and
 5
 6  WHEREAS, some residents are choosing to leave, and the difficulty of finding or
 7   affording housing that meets their needs is a significant factor in that choice; and
 8
 9  WHEREAS, our community values home ownership as a way to maintain stability,
10    build wealth, and feel invested in the long-term health of the community; and
11
12  WHEREAS,  increasing home ownership  includes reducing  cost burdens on
13   residents who rent, allowing renters to build financial assets to purchase a home;
14
15  WHEREAS, our community values diversity, which means not only diversity of
16   residents, but also diversity of homes of many sizes, designs, and price points;
17
18  WHEREAS, the Assembly previously set broad vision for the Municipality in the
19   areas  of economic and  workforce development  in AR 2022-136;  identified
20   actionable strategies to address the community’s housing shortage in AR 2022-416;
21   and adopted Housing among its 2023 priorities in AR 2023-45;
22
23  WHEREAS, AR 2022-416 committed the Assembly to “develop a comprehensive
24   housing policy outlining an Assembly action plan”; and
25
26  WHEREAS, the Assembly will sponsor Housing Action Week in Anchorage from
27   October 30 to November 4, 2023, with a Community Housing Action Summit
28   planned for Friday, November 3, 2023;
29
30  NOW, THEREFORE, THE ANCHORAGE ASSEMBLY RESOLVES:
31
32   Section 1.   The Assembly recognizes the  right of  all people to choose the
33   Municipality of Anchorage as their home.
34
35   Section 2.  The Assembly recognizes  its duty  to weigh the  interests  of  all
36   Anchorage residents, and adopt public policy informed by diverse perspectives.
37
38   Section 3.  The Assembly adopts the following housing policy principles:
39       1. The Municipality strives to be a community with diverse and abundant
40          opportunities for residents to choose a home that meets their needs.
41       2. The Municipality will work to increase opportunities for home ownership by:
42              a. Enacting policies to increase supply of housing for sale;
43              b. Enacting policies to increase supply of rental housing; [and]
44              c. Enacting policies to increase the proportion of resident-occupied
45              housing; and
46              d. Pursuing strategies to reduce housing cost burdens on residents.
47       3. The Municipality cannot unilaterally address  all barriers  in the housing
48         market, but will act locally through plans, policies, and funding decisions to
49          create more favorable market conditions.

AR 2023-260(S): adopting principles to guide housing policy decisions                     Page 3 of 3


 1       4. The Assembly  will support the community to achieve meaningful
 2        progress not through a single policy change, but through shared
 3        commitment and ongoing collaboration to evaluate,  identify, and
 4        remove local barriers.
 5       5. Housing policies will align with the adopted comprehensive plan elements in
 6      AMC Section 21.01.080.
 7
 8   Section 4.  The Assembly will present a housing policy strategic plan at the
 9  Community Housing Action Summit in fall 2023, and work collaboratively with
10   the community to prioritize actionable strategies for the upcoming year.
11
12   Section 5[4]. This resolution shall be effective immediately upon passage and
13   approval by the Assembly.
14
15  PASSED AND APPROVED by the Anchorage Assembly this 22nd day of August,
16   2023.

MUNICIPALITY OF ANCHORAGE

                      ASSEMBLY MEMORANDUM

                                      No. AM 660-2023

                                                  Meeting Date: August 22, 2023

 1   From:     Assembly Member Brawley
 2
 3   Subject:   AR  2023-260(S): A  RESOLUTION OF THE ANCHORAGE
 4           ASSEMBLY RECOGNIZING THE COMMUNITY’S DIVERSE LIVED
 5            EXPERIENCES OF HOUSING  IN THE  MUNICIPALITY OF
 6          ANCHORAGE AND ADOPTING GENERAL PRINCIPLES FOR
 7           FUTURE HOUSING POLICY DECISIONS.
 8
 9   The substitute (S) version of this Resolution incorporates the amendment approved
10    at the August 8, 2023 meeting, as well as recommendations during debate to more
11    clearly connect the policy guidelines in this Resolution with past, current, and future
12   Assembly housing policy work. Specifically, the (S) version refers to prior Assembly
13   resolutions passed in the last year, as well as acknowledging Housing Action Week
14   and the Community Housing Action Summit scheduled for fall 2023.
15
16   The (S) version also connects to an action in AR 2022-416, directing the Assembly
17    to “develop a housing policy and action plan.” This work is underway; the revised
18   Resolution defines this product as a “housing policy strategic plan.” The intent for
19    this plan is a clearly defined vision, goals, and priority actionable strategies. This
20    strategic plan does not replace, and should not conflict with, the vision, goals, and
21   strategies in the Anchorage 2040 Land Use Plan:  it will be compatible with that
22    larger plan, but also help focus the Assembly and community’s energy toward
23   actionable changes that will have a significant positive impact on our multi-faceted
24   housing crisis. The strategic plan will also refer to prior Assembly actions, such as
25   removing minimum parking requirements1 and code reform to encourage accessory
26   dwelling units (ADUs),2 and will reference work already in process, such as the
27   pending ordinance to remove barriers to building 3- and 4-plex housing.
28
29   This Resolution is intended to provide an initial framework to inform the draft housing
30    policy strategic plan, to be presented at the Community Housing Action Summit this
31     fall, and working with the community to choose  priority actions, building on
32   brainstorming at the May 19, 2023 Assembly Housing Retreat, and policy ideas
33   generated through prior Assembly work products.
34
35     I request your support for the (S) version of this Resolution.
36
37   Reviewed by:           Assembly Counsel’s Office
